In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and clinical application of a new treatment regimen for patients with cancer.
the pharmacology and toxicology of cisplatin in combination with interferon.
the development of new therapeutic strategies in cancer treatment using combination chemotherapy and/or immunotherapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
continuous cisplatin infusion with IFN can be safely administered at a dose of 20 mg/m 2 cisplatin per day with IFN given three time weekly.
continuous infusion of cisplatin in combination with IFN is feasible, and that this combination may have a role in the treatment of patients with non-small cell lung carcinoma.
the combination of cisplatin and 3×106 U IFN administered three times a week is tolerable and active in the treatment of advanced non-small cell lung and malignant melanoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of cisplatin and INF is synergistic, but the dose-limiting toxicity of cisplatin is increased when combined with interferon.
the addition of interferon α to continuous infusion cisplat in does not increase renal toxicity, but does significantly increase hematologic toxicity, nausea/vomiting, and protein binding of cisplat.
5-day continuous intravenous infusion cisplatin is well tolerated and has an acceptable toxicity profile.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of 3×106 IFN units with 20 mg/m(2) cisplatin given as a 5-day continuous IV infusion is a safe and tolerable regimen.
the combination of IFN with cisplatin may be a useful strategy for improving the efficacy of cisplatin.
the combination of continuous infusion cisplatine and IFN is synergistic.
